chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “Do not refrain from using the leftover water of the cat to perform wudu (ablution) from it; it is only a beast.”

key_terms.سَبُعٌ: a beast of prey or predatory animal
key_terms.فَضْلَ: leftover remainder, here meaning water remaining after an animal has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu (ablution) with water left over by a cat?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and the permissibility of using water left over by a cat for wudu (ablution). It reflects practical guidance in fiqh on what kinds of water remain usable for purification.
